Figure 2. The Framework of S2 -MLLM. Our model takes sampled multi-view RGB-D frames, related camera parameters, language
descriptions, and the bounding boxes of object proposals as inputs. The shared video encoder and position encoder extract visual and
geometric features from RGB-D frames. The structure-enhanced module (SE) integrates visual features and position information to form
the visual input for the LLM. The Video LLM jointly processes the visual input and the tokenized query, enabling cross-modal under-
standing and reasoning. The grounding head predicts the 3D bounding box (Bbox) of the target object. The language head generates the
category of the target object. while the reconstruction decoder predicts the point map to provide reconstruction supervision. Notice that
the reconstruction is used only at training time.

                                                                              We fine-tune our model based on LLaVA-Video [88] 7B
                                                                              with LoRA [20]. Training is performed across the com-
                                                                              bined dataset for one epoch with a batch size of 8 and a
the combined ScanRefer [9], Nr3D, and Sr3D [2] datasets                       warmup ratio of 0.05. The learning rate is scheduled to
and evaluate it separately, following the setting of [91, 99].                peak for the LLM and for the video encoder during warmup.
This setup enables learning from both natural and template-                   All experiments are conducted only on a single A100 GPU
based expressions while evaluating the model under vary-                      (80GB). The temperature τ for InfoNCE loss is 0.07. Dur-
ing levels of referential complexity. For ScanRefer, we                       ing training, ground-truth bounding boxes are provided as
report accuracy at IoU thresholds of 0.25 and 0.5. For                        object proposals. We employ object proposals generated
ReferIt3D [2], we report results under two settings: (i) us-                  by Mask3D [53] as predicted bounding boxes at inference.
ing ground-truth bounding boxes (GT) as object propos-                        During training, we freeze the reconstruction decoder and
als, which is a commonly used setting in previous meth-                       fine-tune the projection layer, the visual encoder, and the
ods [24, 51], and (ii) using predicted bounding boxes (Pred),                 language model. During inference, the structural guidance
which simulates realistic inference conditions with noisy                     branch is disabled. Please refer to the supplementary for
detections.                                                                   more implementation details.

Figure 3. Qualitative comparison of 3DVG results in challenging spatial understanding cases in 3DVG. Incorrect predictions are highlighted
in magenta, correct ones in cyan, and key spatial relations are underlined. Specifically, S2 -MLLM (a) reasons with scene layout priors.
(b) understands the specified viewpoint. (c) predicts through structure cues despite partial occlusion. (d) distinguishes similar objects
by jointly reasoning over multiple spatial relationships. (e) accurately handles spatial relations involving multiple reference objects. (f)
understands relative positioning. Overall, S2 -MLLM demonstrates more reliable spatial understanding than the previous method.

A. Implementation Details                                                      Table 7. Detailed statistics of hyperparameters.

A.1. Training Details                                                                 Parameter Name                Value
During training, we freeze the reconstruction decoder and                                        Training
fine-tune the projection layer, the visual encoder, and the
language model. Since the LLM output resides in the text                                LoRA rank                     64
space, whereas 3D visual grounding requires regression to                                 LoRA α                      16
region-level features, using LoRA [20] alone is insufficient                           LoRA dropout                  0.05
for learning cross-modal alignment. Therefore, we addi-                                  LoRA bias                  None
tionally fully finetune the last four layers of the LLM, the                          FP/BF Precision                bf16
projection layer, as well as the inter-view and intra-view at-                               tf32                   False
tention during training. The rest of the model is fine-tuned                           weight Decay                   0.0
using LoRA [20], including the visual encoder.                                      tuning MLP or ViT                True
                                                                                       training steps               16928
